item.description: We study the positive geometry of Grassmannians whose boundary is a union of Pl\"ucker divisors. item.title: Correlation functions of 2D critical models via a KPZ relation for conformal blocks
item.description: The Knizhnik--Polyakov--Zamolodchikov (KPZ) relation allows scaling exponents of two-dimensional (2D) critical systems to be derived from their counterparts in Liouville quantum gravity. We extend this framework to correlation functions based on an integral inversion relation between Virasoro conformal blocks with complementary central charges $c$ and $26-c$. We demonstrate this method in various models by deriving the 2-point disk correlation from their quantum counterpart and the KPZ relation. Results on critical loop models were previously known, but our method is robust enough to include many scenarios previously unsolved, such as the Fuzzy Potts model. item.title: The spectrum of codegree Tur\'an densities of 3-graphs
item.description: The \emph{minimum codegree} $\delta_{k-1}(H)$ of a $k$-uniform hypergraph (in short, $k$-graph) $H$ is the smallest number of edges containing a $(k-1)$-set of vertices. For a family $\mathcal{F}$ of $k$-graphs, its \emph{codegree Tur\'an density} $\gamma(\mathcal{F})$ is the asymptotic maximum of $\delta_{k-1}(H)/|V(H)|$ over growing $\mathcal{F}$-free $k$-graphs $H$. We prove that every real number $\alpha\in[0,1)$ is the codegree Tur\'an density of an infinite family $\mathcal{F}_\alpha$ of $3$-graphs, and this family can be chosen so that $\gamma(\mathcal{F}')>\alpha$ for every finite subfamily $\mathcal{F}'\subseteq\mathcal{F}_\alpha$. item.title: A Determinant Proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo Conjecture
item.description: We give an elementary proof of the determinant identity in \cite[Conjecture~A.1]{SYZ} over any field of odd characteristic $p$. The proof computes the determinant of a single linear map by dividing by two different monic polynomials. By \cite[Proposition~A.9]{SYZ}, the identity gives another proof of the Sun--Yang--Zuo conjecture. The conjecture identifies the Higgs--de Rham self-map of the four-pointed projective line with the map induced by multiplication by $p$ on its elliptic double cover. — Jinbang Yang — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: The Riemann Hypothesis and Prime Numbers
item.description: The Riemann hypothesis is attracting a great deal of attention at present. It is one of the seven Millennium Prize Problems in mathematics, for each of which the Clay Mathematics Institute offers a prize of one million dollars. It is arguably the most important open problem in all of mathematics. Numerous results have so far been proved only under the assumption of the Riemann hypothesis. Yet the hypothesis itself sounds rather dull: it conjectures that the zeros of a certain function have a certain form. Things become truly exciting, however, when we look at its connection with prime numbers, and that is what we shall do here. — Stephan Rosebrock — arXiv math.NT / AG / RT

item.title: Moonshine Conjecture Formalized
item.description: The celebrated and intimidating Moonshine Conjecture has now been formalized in Lean. During our formalization project, we repeatedly encountered two problems that a formally checked proof alone does not settle: (1) whether the formal statements actually express the mathematics we humans expect, and (2) how that meaning survives as the repositories and their dependencies evolve. We argue that there is no magic pill that turns a large agent-produced library into mathematics a community can trust. item.description: We now live in the age of machine-generated mathematics: AI systems produce research-level proofs faster than the human mathematical community can read them. Verification is only part of the challenge. We also need to know whether a "new proof" is indeed new, whether a thousand generated proofs contain one idea or many, and where each sits relative to human mathematics. All of these require measuring distances between proofs. item.description: We construct smooth periodic initial data for the three-dimensional incompressible Euler equations whose solution blows up in finite time. Away from the origin, the velocity and its time derivative have smooth spatial limits at the singular time. item.title: Diffusivity and metric exponents for slightly supercritical percolation in high dimensions
item.description: It is a classical fact that random walk on the infinite supercritical Bernoulli $p$-percolation cluster on $\mathbb{Z}^{d}$ converges to Brownian motion with some diffusivity $\sigma(p)$, and that the graph metric on the infinite cluster has order $\mu(p) \|\cdot\|$ at large scales for some constant $\mu(p)$ known as the time constant. item.description: In this paper, we establish sharp Hausdorff dimension and box-counting dimension bounds for sets containing meridian circles and for sets whose difference sets contain a sphere. item.title: On the factorization of Dirac hypergraphs
item.description: A celebrated result from the 70s due to Baranyai states that the complete $k$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices decomposes into perfect matchings if $k\mid n$. item.title: The tower transition in majority bootstrap percolation
item.description: How large must a high-dimensional torus be for majority bootstrap percolation to fill it at a given density below one half? For a torus of side length $n\ge3$, let $H(n)$ be the smallest $h$ such that a tower of $h$ twos has value at least $n$. If $H(n)/d\to\rho\in[0,1]$, the critical density on the $d$-dimensional torus tends to $(1-\rho)/(2-\rho)$. In particular, the smallest side length $n$ for which the critical density is at most $1/4$ satisfies $H(n)\sim 2d/3$. The same curve holds for ordinary boxes of side at least $d$. For boxes with $n/d\to a>0$ we obtain the limiting density $\max\{1/2,1-2^{-1/a}\}$. We determine the first correction to the tower curve away from $\rho=1$. — Vyacheslav Koval, Yuval Peres — arXiv math.AP / CA / PR / DS / arXiv math.CO / LO / cs.CC / cs.DM
